result.topic_en: Completion of the solution expressing x, y, z of the space curve in terms of the parameter p with four arbitrary constants, showing the curve is not planar, eliminating p, and noting the curve is algebraic.
result.transcription:
27

17. Deinde ob $\partial y = p\partial x$ erit nunc $\partial y = -\frac{a(c+p)\partial p}{cp^3}$, cujus integrale praebet $y = \frac{a}{2pp} + \frac{a}{cp} + g$. Pro tertia coordinata $z$ quoniam jam vidimus esse $y + z = \frac{a(c+p)}{cpp}$, erit nunc $z = \frac{a - 2gpp}{2pp} = \frac{a}{2pp} - g$. Hic igitur iterum introductae sunt quatuor constantes arbitrariae; unde intelligitur hanc solutionem esse completam.

18. Hic quidem omnes tres coordinatas $x$, $y$ et $z$ per eandem variabilem $p$ expressas dedimus, id quod pro constructione curvae eundem praestat usum, quoniam pro singulis valoribus loco $p$ assumtis totidem curvae puncta designantur; unde haud difficultur intelligitur totam hanc curvam non in eodem plano esse sitam, propterea quod ex his tribus formulis, elidendo $p$, nulla talis aequatio: $\alpha x + \beta y + \gamma z = 0$ formari potest. Litteram autem $p$ sequenti modo eliminare licebit. Cum sit $y - z = \frac{a}{cp} + 2g$, erit $p = \frac{a}{c(y - z - 2g)}$, qui valor in prima aequatione substitutus producet aequationem inter $x$, $y$ et $z$, cui adjungi poterit ea, quae oritur ex tertia $z + g = \frac{a}{2pp}$, unde fit:
$2a(z + g) = cc(y - z - 2g)^2$.
Verum hae formulae nihil plane conferunt ad curvam describendam. Caeterum evidens est hanc curvam esse algebraicam, secus atque ea quae problemate praecedente erat inventa.

4*

items.quote: Hic igitur iterum introductae sunt quatuor constantes arbitrariae; unde intelligitur hanc solutionem esse completam.
items.english: Here, therefore, four arbitrary constants have again been introduced; whence it is understood that this solution is complete.

items.quote: unde haud difficultur intelligitur totam hanc curvam non in eodem plano esse sitam, propterea quod ex his tribus formulis, elidendo $p$, nulla talis aequatio: $\alpha x + \beta y + \gamma z = 0$ formari potest.
items.english: whence it is easily understood that this whole curve does not lie in one plane, because from these three formulas, by eliminating p, no equation of the form αx + βy + γz = 0 can be formed.

items.quote: Caeterum evidens est hanc curvam esse algebraicam, secus atque ea quae problemate praecedente erat inventa.
items.english: Moreover it is evident that this curve is algebraic, unlike the one found in the preceding problem.
